leads_to.evidence: An ACS survey of new chemistry graduates found about a third went straight on to graduate or professional school, including Ph.D., medical and pharmacy programs. Slightly more than a third held full-time jobs, so first-year pay leaves out many graduates.

nearby_pair.evidence: No nearby pair was identified for this major.

school_matters.evidence: Chemistry has no license, and the typical first job at any school is lab or quality-control work. An ACS survey found new bachelor's chemists' starting pay closely bunched, and the four admission bands sit within a narrow range of each other.

who_is_counted.evidence: None of the major's programs is online-only or pooled. Chemistry degrees require years of in-person lab courses taken full time, so the largest programs enroll traditional students rather than working adults.

programs.evidence: The Oakland campus reports the same earnings, debt and cohort as Northeastern's Boston campus, so its figures are Boston's chemistry graduates pooled under another campus.
Northeastern's chemistry degree includes two or three paid co-op work terms in industry before graduation, so its graduates start their careers with job experience.
The cohort is small. Baton Rouge also has one of Louisiana's largest groups of chemical plant and refinery jobs, including ExxonMobil's chemist roles, which may help explain the high pay.
